messages:
mike_g: Hey team — quick q: I added my newborn to Redwood benefits last week but my partner actually already has coverage. Can I remove the baby from our plan? Is there a deadline or any payroll consequences I should know about?

annelise (People Ops): Congrats Mike! :tada: You can remove a dependent outside of open enrollment. If the dependent was added recently because of a qualifying life event (birth), there are a couple of things to note:
1) Removal itself is allowed anytime, but refunds/retro adjustments depend on payroll timing.
2) If you want premiums refunded for future pay periods, we can process that; retro refunds for pay periods already run may take an extra payroll cycle to show up.
3) Required step: submit the Dependent Change Form and indicate reason ("Other coverage"), and attach proof of other coverage if available.

mike_g: Thanks — where do I find that form? Do I need to re-enter anything in Rippling?

annelise (People Ops): Two ways:
- Preferred: Email benefits@redwood.com with subject `Dependent removal — [your name]` and attach the Dependent Change Form (PDF) plus any supporting docs (insurance card from partner/COBRA paperwork).
- Alternate: In Rippling go to Benefits → Manage Dependents → Remove dependent, but we still ask for the form/email so Benefits has a record.
Link to internal doc: https://intranet.redwood.com/benefits/adding-removing-dependents (contains form and examples).

jamal (Benefits): Quick technicals: if you added the newborn during the 30-day special enrollment window after birth, removal is fine. We mark the removal effective as-of the date you request unless you ask for a specific future date. If a payroll run already occurred covering the period, we will queue an adjustment; typically it posts within 1–2 pay cycles.

payroll-bot: Note from Payroll: Changes submitted before the payroll cutoff (Wednesdays 11:59pm PT) will be reflected in the next run. Changes after cutoff are processed on the following run and any refunds/charges are batched.

olivia: FWIW — I removed my kid when we found better coverage through my spouse. I emailed benefits, attached their insurance card, and the refund showed up as a positive adjustment two cycles later. No tax paperwork needed on our end.

mike_g: Got it — I'll email benefits@redwood.com now with the form + partner insurance card. Do I need the baby's SSN to remove them?

jamal (Benefits): You don't need SSN to remove. SSN is only required when adding a dependent (for carrier enrollment and tax reporting). For removal, proof of other coverage or a statement works.

annelise (People Ops): Also remember open enrollment is coming up (Nov 1–14) if you want to re-evaluate plans. If you remove now and later want to add back outside open enrollment, you'd need a qualifying event or wait for open enrollment.

mike_g: Perfect — thanks everyone. Sending the email and form in a minute.

jamal (Benefits): Copying the checklist here to make it quick: 1) Dependent Change Form (signed) 2) Proof of other coverage (insurance card/letter) 3) Email to benefits@redwood.com with subject `Dep removal - [EmployeeName]` 4) Confirm desired effective date (today or future)

mike_g: Done — emailed with attachments. cc'd payroll in case they need it.

payroll-bot: Received: benefits request 1768256789. Status: queued for review.

olivia: Nice — keep an eye on Benefits status in Rippling, they update there too once completed. :+1: 

mike_g: Thanks all, really appreciate the quick help!
